questions.q: How many letters arrive from Johannesburg, and which one does Kumalo open first, 'fearfully'?
choices: Four — and he opens Mr Carmichael's first, because it will be about the mercy
questions.explain: The others are from Absalom (to his wife and to his parents) and from Msimangu.

questions.q: What does Mr Carmichael's letter say?
choices: That there will be an appeal
That there will be no mercy, and Absalom will be hanged on the fifteenth day of that month
questions.explain: Kumalo sits 'an hour, two hours maybe', seeing and hearing nothing.

questions.q: How does Kumalo's wife respond to the news?
choices: She reads it, sits briefly with 'lost and terrible eyes', then stands: 'It is not good to sit idle' — and sends him to visit the sick
questions.explain: 'This was the child of her womb, of her breasts.'

questions.q: In his letter, what does Absalom say about Ndotsheni?
choices: That he never wants to go back
That he will not see it again — 'if I were back there I should not leave it again'
That he blames his home for what happened
questions.explain: A black priest from Pretoria is preparing him and speaks well to him.

questions.q: What is the 'business of the sticks' that a survey party plants in the valley?
questions.explain: The magistrate, Jarvis and other white men set up sticks and flags while the chief looks on, not understanding.

questions.q: What breaks over the valley the same day the sticks are planted?
choices: A great storm — the drought breaks at last, with thunder and heavy rain
questions.explain: Jarvis had said, 'This'll be no ordinary storm.'

questions.q: Where does Jarvis take shelter during the downpour?
choices: In Kumalo's church — where 'the roof leaks in many places'
questions.explain: They sit in near-darkness while the rain drums on the iron roof.

questions.q: What does Jarvis quietly ask Kumalo in the church, and how does he respond to the answer?
choices: 'Is there mercy?' — Kumalo hands him Carmichael's letter; Jarvis reads it and says he understands, and 'When it comes to this fifteenth day... I shall remember'
Whether the dam site is right
questions.explain: 'I do not understand these matters, but otherwise I understand completely.'

questions.q: How does Kumalo behave toward Jarvis as he leaves the church?
choices: He is too overcome to say 'go well', to carry the saddle, or to thank Jarvis for the milk
questions.explain: The valley is now 'full of sound, of streams and rivers, all red with the blood of the earth.'

questions.q: What happens with the survey sticks after the storm?
choices: Children play at pulling them out; Dazuma's young son pulls one out in error, and the men carefully replace it so no one can tell
questions.explain: The chief had ordered that not one stick be touched or removed.
